answer: Staking bonds resist sybils: each agent must lock collateral before submitting work or voting, and that deposit is slashed on dishonest behavior. The stake acts as a beacon of commitment honest agents recover on completion. To forge a thousand fake identities, an attacker must lock a thousand deposits at once, so cost scales linearly with fake count instead of staying near zero. Every new identity is an inlet for capital that cannot be reused elsewhere. When slashed stake exceeds what a fake can extract, mass forgery becomes unprofitable and the network stays cheap for real agents.
